name: requirement_vs_baseline
description: Requirement themes with their lost rate set against the sub-account's OWN baseline lost rate, plus whether the deal moved stage after a rep replied. Use for 'what is actually blocking deals', 'which customer asks are roadblocks', 'what do customers ask for right before they go quiet'. THE TEST THIS VIEW EXISTS FOR: a theme is only a roadblock where its lost_rate_pct is ABOVE baseline_lost_rate_pct AND deals did not move after it was raised. Frequency alone proves nothing — the most-mentioned theme is usually just the most common thing customers say. Both numbers are on every row so the comparison needs no second query; state both when calling something a blocker. A theme below baseline is evidence AGAINST it being a problem, and worth saying so when someone assumes otherwise. moved_stage_after and no_move_after come from replies linked to that specific requirement; where both are 0 no rep reply was linked and the movement test cannot be applied — say that rather than reading 0 as 'never moved'. stage_at_time is the stage the deal was at when the customer said it, so the same theme appears on several rows, one per stage.

params.name: requirement
params.description: Only requirement themes matching this text.

params.name: stage
params.description: Only things said while the deal was at this stage.

params.name: min_asked
params.description: Only themes asked on at least this many deals. A lost rate over 2 or 3 deals is noise.

params.name: min_lost_rate
params.description: Only themes whose lost rate is at least this percentage. Compare against baseline_lost_rate_pct on the same row, never against a number from elsewhere.

params.name: min_no_move
params.description: Only themes where at least this many replies were followed by no stage movement.
